questions.question: In India, Inflation is measured by the ________.
questions.solution:
Inflation

 
 
 
It is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and Services.

 
 
 

 
 
Retail inflation

 
 
 
Measured in term of CPI(Consumer Price Index)

 
 
 

 
 
Wholesale inflation

 
 
 
Measured in term of WPI(wholesale price index)

 
 
 

 
 
Outcome of Inflation

 
 
 
Inflation provide benefits to debtors and loss to creditors/bondholders.

 
Limited inflation is good for growth in developing country.

 
 
 

 
 
**Consumer Price Index (CPI)**

 
 
 
**Measure that examines the weighted average of prices of a basket of consumer goods and services, such as transportation, food and medical care.**

questions.question: India is a Union of States. Executive power of the Union is vested in the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The executive power of the Union is vested in the President, and according to the Constitution is exercised by him either directly or through officers subordinate to him**__. The supreme command of the Defense Forces of the Union also vests in him.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The President summons, prorogues, addresses, sends messages to the Parliament and dissolves the Lok Sabha, issues ordinances at any time except when both the Houses of Parliament are in session, makes recommendations for the introduction of Financial and Money Bills, and grants, grants clemency, in certain cases remits, relieves or suspends or suspends punishment, and commutes or commutes punishment.
 
• When there is a failure of the constitutional machinery in a state, he can take over all or any of the functions of the government of that state.
 
• The President can declare an emergency in the country if he is satisfied that a serious emergency exists, which threatens the security of India or any part of its territory, whether by war or external aggression or armed rebellion.

questions.question: Hampi is situated in which state?
questions.solution:

questions.question: Who was the last Mughal Emperor?
questions.solution:
• Bahadur Shah Zaffar was the last Emperor to sit on the throne of India.
 
• Bahadur Shah Zafar was the last Mughal emperor of India who was born in 1775 at Delhi.
 
• He ascended the throne at a very advanced age, after the death of his father, in 1837. He was last ruler of the Mughal Dynasty, which ruled India for about 300 years. He did not rule over his empire with a strong hand because of the rising power of the British.

questions.question: Through which of the following countries does the river Tigris flow?
questions.solution:
__
 
• Tigris River flows through **Iraq**__.
 
• The river flows south from the mountains of south eastern Turkey through Iraq and empties itself into the Persian Gulf.
 
• The Tigris is the eastern member of the two great rivers that define Mesopotamia, the other being the Euphrates.

questions.question: What name was assigned to the world’s ﬁrst clone of an adult animal by British scientists?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dolly.**__

 
• Dolly was a female domestic sheep and the first mammal cloned from an adult somatic cell, using the process of nuclear transfer.
 
• She was cloned at the Roslin Institute in Midlothian, Scotland and lived there until her death when she was six years old.
 
• The technique that was made famous by her birth is somatic cell nuclear transfer, in which a cell is placed in a de-nucleated ovum, the two cells fuse and then develop into an embryo.

questions.question: In which process plants convert potential energy into kinetic energy?
questions.solution:
__**​​Explanation:**__

__
 
• Plants prepare their food by the process called **photosynthesis. **
 
• During photosynthesis, plants trap solar energy or light energy with the help of chloroplast present in the green leaves and convert it into Chemical energy

• This chemical energy stored in plants can be considered as the **potential energy** now when any animal eats the plants this stored potential energy is used by the animal in the form of** kinetic energy** as the animal can move** **

questions.question: How many chromosomes are there in human body?
questions.solution:
• ​In humans, each cell normally contains 23 pairs of chromosomes, for a total of 46.
 
• Twenty-two of these pairs, called autosomes, look the same in both males and females.
 
• The 23rd pair, the sex chromosomes, differ between males and females. Females have two copies of the X chromosome, while males have one X and one Y chromosomes.

questions.question: In which year did Yuri Gagarin take the ﬁrst travel in Space?
questions.solution:
• Yuri Gargarin of Soviet Union became the first human to travel into outer space when his Vostok spacecraft completed one orbit of the Earth on 12 April 1961.
 
• His flight, on April 12, 1961, lasted 108 minutes as he circled the Earth for a little more than one orbit
 
• Gagarin's flight came at a time when the United States and the Soviet Union were competing for technological supremacy in space during Cold War.

questions.question: Why does the oil move up in the lamp?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Capillary action**__.

__CONCEPT__:

 
• Capillarity: If a tube of the very narrow bore (called capillary) is dipped in a liquid, it is found that the liquid in the capillary either ascends or descends relative to the surrounding liquid. This phenomenon is called capillarity.
 
• The root cause of capillarity is the difference in pressures on two sides of the (concave and convex) curved surface of the liquid.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/fe6d8e50e4593a64912878e3c15916d9d2f96f114503286f78875e506d63d603.png] 

 
• Capillary action draws the ink to the tips of fountain pen nibs from a reservoir or cartridge within the pen.
 
• This thread used in lanterns is also known as the wick and because of the capillary action of liquid kerosene keeps rising in a wick and helps it burn.

questions.question: All the machinery and equipment of computer are called ________.
questions.solution:
• ​All the machinery and equipment of computer are called Hardware.
 
• Computer hardware includes the physical, tangible parts or components of a computer, such as the central processing unit, monitor, keyboard, computer data storage, graphic card, sound card, speakers and motherboard.

questions.question: Which of the following acids destroys bacteria in stomach?
questions.solution:
• The acid which help us to digest food and is present in our stomach is HCL.
 
• Hydrochloric acid activates pepsinogen into the enzyme pepsin, which then helps digestion by breaking the bonds linking amino acids, a process known as proteolysis.
 
• Gastric acid, gastric juice or stomach acid, is a digestive fluid formed in the stomach and is composed of hydrochloric acid, potassium chloride and sodium chloride

questions.question: How many times an adult breathes approximately in one minute?
questions.solution:
• An average adult breaths almost 16-18 times in a minute.
 
• Toddlers might breathe 20-30 times per minute.
 
• A respiration rate under 12 or over 25 breaths per minute while resting is considered abnormal.

questions.question: Layer which saves life from harmful effects of UV radiations is known as ________.
questions.solution:
• The column of atmosphere is divided into five different layers depending upon the temperature condition. They are: troposphere, stratosphere, mesosphere, ionosphere and exosphere.
 
• One important feature of the stratosphere is that it contains the ozone layer. The stratosphere is found above the tropopause and extends up to a height of 50 km.
 
• This layer absorbs ultra-violet radiation and shields life on the earth from intense, harmful form of energy.

questions.question: Who was the inventor of X-rays?
questions.solution:
• X-Rays was invented by W.C Roentgen.
 
• X-rays were discovered in 1895 by Wilhelm Conrad Roentgen (1845-1923) who was a Professor at Wurzburg University in Germany.
 
• X-Ray is an electromagnetic wave of high energy and very short wavelength, which is able to pass through many materials opaque to light.

questions.question: How much amount is given as a reward under the Dadasaheb Phalke Award?
questions.solution:
• **Rs. 10 Lacs **are given alongside the Dadasaheb Phalke Award.
 
• The Dadasaheb Phalke Award is India's highest award in cinema. It is presented annually at the National Film Awards ceremony by the Directorate of Film Festivals, an organisation set up by the Ministry of Information and Broadcasting.
 
• The award comprises a Swarna Kamal (Golden Lotus) medallion, a shawl, and a cash prize of Rs. 10 Lakh.
 
• Most recent winner of this award is actor **Shri Rajinikanth in 2019.**

questions.question: Who is the author of the famous poem "Kamayani"?
questions.solution:
• Jaishankar Prasad wrote the famous poem Kamayani in 1936.
 
• Kamayani is a Hindi epic poem by Jaishankar Prasad. It is considered one of the greatest literary works written in modern times in Hindi literature.

questions.question: With which country India signed agreement to improve grid integration of renewable energy?
questions.solution:
• Germany and India signed agreement to improve grid integration of renewable energy on August 2017.
 
• India and Germany signed an agreement on technical cooperation under the Indo-German Energy Programme – Green Energy Corridors (IGEN-GEC).
 
• The main objective of this programme component is to improve the sector framework and conditions for grid integration of renewable energy.

questions.question: India agrees to boost joint infra projects with which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
• India agreed to boost joint infra projects with Nepal in August 2017.
 
• The two Countries pledged to pursue new opportunities to further deepen bilateral relations for the benefit of the peoples of both countries while committing to further reinvigorate the existing mechanisms.
 
• The project include railways, roadways, and transportation etc.
